item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is materially closer to the frozen contract because it keeps the change scoped to Files.Upload and reuses multipartbody.NewFile. B adds a prohibited global retry/body-buffering refactor and changes Files.Add behavior.","reasons":["Both patches incorrectly duplicate FilesService.Add’s request/response logic instead of routing Upload through Add, but A is substantially easier to bring into contract.","A preserves the existing Add implementation and avoids unrelated retry-transport changes.","B changes RawClient.Do semantics for every non-native io.Reader, including eagerly consuming and buffering bodies and surfacing read errors before sending; this conflicts with the explicit requirements to preserve Add behavior and avoid retry refactoring.","B’s changelog and README advertise the out-of-contract global buffering behavior, increasing the cleanup required before merge."],"risks_a":["Upload does not call FilesService.Add, duplicating option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data behavior.","Tests omit the explicitly requested validation and source-reader-error cases.","The retry test does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods: true and uses a strings.Reader rather than demonstrating a streamed/opaque source."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its machinery.","The RawClient.Do change is explicitly outside scope and changes behavior globally, not just for Upload.","Global eager buffering can increase memory use, delay requests, and alter error timing for existing callers, including Files.Add and Files.Update despite the contract requiring unchanged behavior."]}
